children: Snowflake lifted its full-year forecast for product revenue after recording a narrower second-quarter loss, as artificial intelligence continued to drive its business.
The cloud storage company on Wednesday reported a loss of $191.7 million, or 55 cents a share, compared with a loss of $298 million, or 89 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, the company reported earnings of 62 cents a share, ahead of analysts' estimates of 45 cents a share, according to FactSet.
Shares recently jumped 22.9% to $376 in after-hours trading.
Revenue rose to $1.55 billion, up from $1.14 billion a year earlier. Analysts surveyed by FactSet were expecting $1.48 billion in revenue.
Product revenue, which makes up 96% of the company's total revenue, was $1.49 billion.
Snowflake added 692 net new customers during the latest quarter, up 32% from a year earlier.
"AI continues to compound our advantages, creating a flywheel effect across the business," Chief Executive Sridhar Ramaswamy said.
For the current third quarter, the company is projecting product revenue between $1.588 billion and $1.593 billion. Analysts were targeting product revenue of $1.50 billion, according to FactSet.

Snowflake is expecting full-year product revenue of about $6.07 billion, representing 31% year-over-year growth. Analysts were targeting $5.85 billion. The company previously expected product revenue of $5.84 billion for the year.
